verdict:
The stage is still split in two. The cold dining frames (dining, dining_gene, chair, chair_gene) are near fern level. The new screen cameras are not, and tv is the weakest frame in the set.

tv reads as a grey card on a grey wall, not as a television in a family's room. The panel takes 64 % of the frame width with only 6 % keystone, so it is almost frontal. The panel is raw 143 against a raw wall of 63-74, only about twice the wall's code value. Graded, it is 123 against about 50 on the left and 29 on the right. It adds almost nothing to the room:
- "TV blank panel" is a 0.68-strength emitter with emission_sampling NONE, and no spill light exists. The wall it hangs on is in the same plane as the panel, so it could not catch the panel's light anyway.
- The wall is brightest at the lower left, away from the TV (raw 74 falling to about 51-55 at the right), so it is lit by the window fills (d_sky_end, d_sky).
- Because the camera has framing="dining", it also inherits the dining haze (0.012) and trims. The haze is not what greys the case, though. The bezel grades 35-38 while the cabinet's shaded edge right beside it grades 17-22 under the same haze. Most of the lift is the case's broad sheen (roughness 0.51) reflecting the lit room.
- The only neighbours are part of a picture frame cut at x≈165, a candle stub cut by the bottom edge, and the corner wall as a dark band on the right. The picture frame reads as a second dark screen and shows a black overlap square at its corner.
With real hearing or NBC footage laid in, this becomes a picture-in-picture, not a scene.

kitchen_over is a sound over-the-shoulder. The screen clearly lights the hands, the palm rest, the rim of Dawn's neck and the side of the mug. But:
- The kitchen is missing: 21 % of the lower-right quadrant and 13 % of the upper-right grade below 8.
- The aluminium deck competes with the screen: the trackpad grades 178 and the palm rest about 165 against the screen's 190 (196-200 against 205 in the raw).
- The hands are fanned wide with nearly straight fingers over the keys, and the right hand sits on the keyboard, not the trackpad. This is the spread-finger fault the last critique named in dining_family.

For the insert job, both panels are flat in the raw (std 0.4 and 1.7), and the corner JSONs match the rendered edges to under a pixel, which is good. But both are pure emitters with no glass at all. The grade's vignette, not the render, darkens the TV panel from about 140 near the frame centre to about 85 at its right edge. Inserts must therefore go into the raw plates before the grade, and both screens need a separate glass pass to look like glass.

Not pro yet. First make the TV light the room and place it in the room.
answers:
1) How do the screens read in the room?

TV: it does not read in a room.
- The frame is the panel: about 810 x 465 px, 64 % of the width. It is almost frontal: the left edge is 478 px tall against 448 on the right.
- It is not a light source. Panel to wall is raw 143 to 63-74, only about 2:1 in code value. Graded, it is 123 to about 50 on the left and 29 on the right.
- The wall's brightest area is at the bottom left, away from the TV. Raw row 660 runs from 74 to 55, left to right, and the right gap averages 51. The light comes from d_sky_end and d_sky, not from the TV.
- "TV blank panel" in home_set.television() has emission_sampling NONE and no area light, so it adds almost no light. The only surface around it is the wall, which is in the same plane and cannot catch its light. Nothing in this frame stands in front of the TV to show its light.
- The neighbours make it worse:
  - The picture frame cut at x 0-165 reads as a second dark screen.
  - A candle stub is cut at x 110-132 by the bottom edge.
  - The x0 corner wall is a dark band (graded 13) at the right edge.
- The cabinet's edge is 15 cm from the side wall. It overlaps the end of the sideboard by 14-17 cm (body and top) and sits 15 cm from the picture. A wider angle will show it crammed into the corner.
- Through framing="dining", this shot also inherits the dining haze (HAZE['dining'] = 0.012) and the dining trims. The haze is only a minor part of the grey bezel (see 2).

Laptop: it reads well as the light source.
- The panel grades 190. The right hand reaches p95 178, the trackpad 178 and the palm rest about 165. The right rim of the neck is lit (up to 95) and the mug's inner side catches the light, against a surround of 8-23.
- What it lacks is the room. The area above the lid averages 23 and the area right of the lid 9. Only the mug and the envelope corner say "kitchen at night".
- The trackpad and palm rest, at 165-178, are the second-brightest shape and nearly match the screen, which weakens the "one light" read.

2) How clearly do the bezels separate from the surroundings?

TV: the bezel separates, but softly.
- Graded profiles:
  - Left (row 330): wall 49-54, then an 8-10 px dark outline at 17-22 (the cabinet's bevelled edge and its shadow on the wall), then the bezel at 35-38, then the panel at 113-118 within one pixel.
  - Top: wall 50-52, dark line 18-20, bezel 35-38, panel 121-125.
  - Bottom: panel 130, bezel 39-42, dark line 18-30, wall 60.
  - Right: panel 89, bezel 18-19, dark line 10-12, wall 33-34.
- The bezel is about 10 px wide at the left and top, 8 px at the right and 17 px at the bottom.
- On the left, top and bottom the bezel is only 1.4-1.5:1 under the wall, so it reads as a grey frame on a blue-grey wall, not as a black TV. On the right it is about 1.8:1.
- The cause is mostly the case's own sheen. The shaded edge next to the bezel grades 17-22 under the same haze, so the haze adds at most about that much. The front face (base 0.016, roughness 0.51) picks up the rest as a broad reflection of the lit room. With the room fills cut and the haze off, the case should fall toward the 17-22 that the edge shows. If it does not, lower the case roughness.
- The panel sits 2 mm proud of the cabinet face (panel at TV y, cabinet front at y-0.002). Real panels are recessed behind the bezel. This is invisible at this angle but will show in a wider one.

Laptop: clean on three sides, weak on the left.
- Bottom: panel 190-198, then bezel 12-14.
- Right: bezel about 80 (a gloss reflection), lid edge 66-74, void 8-9.
- Top: void 27-30, dark line 14-15, bezel 40-50.
- Left: bezel 26-34 against a void of 13-15, about 2:1. This is the weakest side: the lid's left edge reads only faintly, and the screen's own edge defines it.

Both corner JSONs are accurate to under 1 px:
- TV: the top edge at x 700 is predicted at 98.7 and measured at 98-99. The left edge at y 330 is predicted at 321.7 and measured at 321-322.
- Laptop: the right edge at y 280 is predicted at 858.4 and measured at about 858.5. The bottom at x 650 is predicted at 416.9 and measured at about 417.

3) Is there room for a slow push with all four corners visible?

TV: yes, numerically.
- An 8 % push about the frame centre puts TR at (1173, 85), TL at (294, 72) and BL at (298, 588). All margins stay at 72 px or more, and the cabinet's outer edge stays in.
- The limit is the right edge, at about 29 %.
- It will still read as a 2D zoom on a flat wall. The wall is at 1.80-1.94 m with nothing in front of it, and 8 % is a dolly of about 0.14 m with no parallax. The push needs a foreground layer.
- The panel is off centre: its centre is at (726, 331).
- The grade's vignette (shoot.py, vignette=angle=PI/4.4) takes the flat raw 143 to about 140 near the frame centre, about 118 at the panel's left edge and about 85 at its right edge (78 in the darkest corner).
- An insert laid on the graded frame will not match. Composite into the raw and regrade, or centre the TV.

Laptop: plenty of room.
- Corners span x 435-870 and y 136-442. An 8 % push leaves 118 px or more at the top, and the corners stay in up to about 60 %.
- There are two real problems.
  - (a) At 8 % the panel is about 440 px wide, too small for an email body to be read. Only a large subject line or a single highlighted phrase will read, so the email needs its own insert angle or a much longer push.
  - (b) Dawn's head and shoulder are much nearer the lens than the screen. From the stage geometry, her shoulder is roughly 0.8 m away (camera at y 1.13, her chair at y 0.6) and the screen 1.3 m. Depth parallax from a single still will tear at the shoulder edge over the hands and keyboard. It needs a clean plate without Dawn, or a real rendered move.

4) Lead note, the insert job:
- Flat enough: yes. Raw std is 0.4 on the TV and 1.7 on the laptop.
- Dark enough: only for a replace composite. The TV panel is a mid grey of 143 and the laptop a near white of 205, which is wrong for an additive or screen composite.
- Glass reflection: there is none. Both screens are pure emission shaders with no specular, so nothing fights the insert, but nothing sells glass either. The insert will look like a sticker.
- Light source when lit: the laptop works. The TV does not, and its spill should match the average of the footage (a hearing room's mid grey, not white).
- If the NBC clip carries the network's bug or chyrons, those are a source credit and labels on the shot. DECISIONS' on-screen labels rule forbids them ("No source credits on shots"). Crop or scale the footage inside the panel so that neither shows, and do the same for any caption burned into the hearing video.

fixes.problem: The TV adds almost no light, and the room around it is lit by other sources. The panel is only about twice the wall's code value (raw 143 vs 63-74), so it cannot read as the room's light source.
fixes.fix:
1. In home.py, generalise screen_light(scr) to screen_light(scr, size, energy, name), registering st.LIGHTS under that name. Call it for bpy.data.objects['television_screen'] with name 'tv_spill', size (0.86, 0.48), energy about 25 W (tune it), colour (0.78, 0.86, 1.0), spread_deg 120 and visible_camera False. The panel's normal faces +Y, into the room, so the function's placement works unchanged.
2. Default tv_spill to 0 in apply_camera(), the way family_pendant is: trims = dict(TRIMS.get(framing, {}), family_pendant=0.0, tv_spill=0.0). The dining and chair frames show the Ch 10 room with the TV off.
3. Give CAMERAS['tv'] its own framing='tv', with TRIMS['tv'] = {'tv_spill': 1.0, 'd_sky_end': 0.3, 'd_sky': 0.25, 'street': 0.3, 'street_side': 0.3} and HAZE['tv'] = 0.0. It currently inherits the dining trims and the 0.012 haze.
4. Targets on the graded frame: wall beside the TV at 18-25, case and bezel at 12-20, panel to wall at 4:1 or more. If the case stays grey with the fills down, lower its roughness from 0.51, because its sheen spreads the room's light over the whole face.
5. The wall is in the panel's plane and will not take its light. In the re-framed shot (next fix), the sideboard top, the brass candlesticks and the foreground chair back should be the brightest non-screen surfaces, at 60-90 on the faces turned to the TV.

fixes.problem: The frame is the panel with the room cropped away: a frontal grey card beside part of a picture frame (which reads as a second screen), a cut candle stub and a dark corner band. A push on a flat wall at 1.9 m has no parallax and reads as a 2D zoom.
fixes.fix:
1. Re-frame it as a shot inside the dining room. Put the camera back and lower, about 25-30 degrees off the TV's normal from the sideboard (+X) side, with a dark dining-chair back soft in the near foreground at 0.6-0.9 m. The near (-Y) side of the table has no chair (chair_n2 was removed for the dining wide; see the note under DINING_CHAIRS in home_set.py), so add a copy of a dining chair that renders only for this camera.
2. Include the full sideboard end, with both candlesticks catching the TV spill. Keep the picture either wholly in frame or wholly out. From the start below, its left member and the candlesticks fall about 20 degrees off axis, at the left edge of a 35-40 mm frame, so swing the aim or change the lens until they clear the edge or sit well inside.
3. Start from about loc (2.6, -0.6, 1.25), aim (1.62, -2.245, 1.45), lens 35-40, f/4. Have frame_metadata check that all four corners are in_frame at both the start and the end of an 8 % dolly.
4. Keep the current tight angle as a second camera, tv_insert, aimed at the panel centre (aim = st.TV). That puts the panel centre on (640, 360), so the vignette falls symmetrically on the insert. Give it framing='tv', and add 'tv_insert' to frame_metadata()'s screen map so it writes its own corners JSON.

fixes.problem: Both screens are pure emitters with no specular, so a composited insert will look like a sticker. The grade's vignette, applied after rendering, darkens the TV panel from about 140 near the frame centre to about 85 at its right edge, while the raw is flat.
fixes.fix:
1. Add a glass pass. Behind an env flag (e.g. HOME_SCREEN_OFF=1), replace the emission on 'TV blank panel' and 'screen' with a Principled surface: base (0.005, 0.005, 0.006), roughness 0.04-0.06, IOR 1.5, coat 0. Leave the spill lights on, and render the same camera again to the same corners.
2. Composite on the raw PNG. Insert the footage by its corners, then add the glass pass over it inside the panel matte, starting at its rendered strength and trimming to taste.
3. Then apply the A-fixed grade, the GRADE chain in scenes/shoot.py, so the vignette and grain fall on the insert too. scenes/regrade_frames.sh applies that chain to stills; for a moving insert, run the same ffmpeg chain on the composited frames.
4. Scale the TV spill to the insert's mean luminance: about 0.35 of a white panel's energy for hearing footage.

fixes.problem: The hands are fanned wide, with nearly straight fingers over the keys. CURL extends every joint 4-14 degrees past Rigify's relaxed curl, and nothing closes MakeHuman's rest fan. The right hand sits on the right half of the keyboard instead of on the trackpad, where the stage's own brief puts 'a finger on the trackpad'. Dawn is reading, not typing, and her right hand is the brightest skin in frame (p95 178 graded).
fixes.fix:
1. In home.py, change CURL and HANDS (lines 316-330), curl_fingers() and arms_on_table() (lines 504-546) so the right hand rests on the trackpad. The heel of the palm sits on the palm rest, the index lies slightly extended on the pad, and the other fingers curl 30-40 degrees at MCP and PIP.
2. Rest the left hand's heel on the palm rest, left of the trackpad. Curl its fingers 25-30 degrees, with the pads on the home row and the thumb by the space bar.
3. Close the fan with articulate_hand's fourth value (spread in the palm plane, positive toward the thumb), e.g. index -8, ring +5, pinky +10. curl_fingers() passes only three values today, so extend it.
4. The wrists should sit 15-25 mm above the deck. The existing debug line in table_things() prints wrist heights over the table top; also print them over the deck.
5. Verify from both kitchen and kitchen_over, since they share Dawn. The laptop is placed under the hands, so its corners JSON will change with the pose.

fixes.problem: There is no kitchen behind the laptop. Above the lid averages 23 graded and right of the lid 9, and 21 % of the lower-right quadrant grades below 8. The shot reads as a laptop in a black void.
fixes.fix:
1. On the wall the camera faces (K y0 = -2.4, about 3.5 m away and defocused at f/3.5, bare today), add one practical shape: a half-open doorway with a thin vertical strip of warm hall light. Make it either an emissive slit 0.04 x 1.9 m at strength about 0.6, or a dim area light raking the door edge. Place it so it lands in the frame's upper right, behind the lid's right edge.
2. Target 25-45 graded for that shape. Lift the table top right of the laptop from about 13 to 20-30 with the existing screen_spill or a small cool bounce.
3. Keep it soft and dim, so the screen stays the room's light and the strip reads as light from beyond the room. It is context, not a second subject.

fixes.problem: The aluminium deck nearly matches the screen: the trackpad grades 178 and the palm rest about 165 against the screen's 190 (196-200 against 205 in the raw). The metallic deck mirrors the screen above it.
fixes.fix:
Make the laptop a darker, unbranded space grey:
1. In home_set.materials(), give 'alu' (mt.aluminium, base 0.28 today) a base of about 0.18-0.22 and roughness of 0.4 or more. 'alu' also covers the lid and hinge, so check the lid's back in kitchen.
2. Darken 'trackpad' (base 0.2 today, metallic 0.6) to a base of 0.12.
3. Target the palm rest at 90-120 graded, so the screen is the single brightest shape and the hands are second.

fixes.problem: The email cannot be read at this size: the panel is about 440 px wide at 1280, even after an 8 % push. Dawn's head and shoulder, much nearer the lens than the screen, will tear in a depth-parallax push from one still.
fixes.fix:
1. Add a camera, kitchen_screen: a near-square-on insert over Dawn's right shoulder, with the panel filling about 70 % of the frame width (lens 85, focus fx_screen, f/2.8). Keep the hands' tips soft at the bottom edge. Add it to frame_metadata()'s screen map so it writes its own corners JSON.
2. For kitchen_over, render a clean plate at the same camera with Dawn hidden at render time (hide_render on _STATE['cast']), not with --nocast. Without the cast, table_things() puts the laptop at its default spot instead of under her hands, so a --nocast plate would not line up.
3. shoot.py writes no depth pass today. Add a Z pass so the parallax push can fill what the moving shoulder reveals.
4. Alternatively, render the move itself: a real 0.1 m dolly along the view axis, rendered here on the CPU with no paid GPU time.

fixes.problem: The picture frame shows a black square at its corner (about x 120-155, y 585-620). d_frameL/R (0.72 tall) overlap d_frameT/B (0.92 wide) in 5 x 5 cm blocks with coincident front faces. The TV panel also sits 2 mm proud of its cabinet's front face (panel at TV y, cabinet front at TV y - 0.002).
fixes.fix:
1. In home_set.dining(), make the L/R members 0.62 tall (fz plus or minus 0.31) so they butt between T and B, or mitre them. Afterwards check chair and chair_gene, which show the same picture with the same small squares at its lower corners.
2. In television(), give the panel a real recess. The cabinet is a solid box, so the panel cannot simply move behind its front face. Keep the panel where it is, so its corners JSON stays valid, and add a 4-5 mm bezel lip. Use four thin bars of the case material around the panel's edge, standing out to about TV y + 0.004, so the lip shades the panel's edge.

fixes.problem: kitchen.jpg dates from 27 November and is older than the current code. Its right index finger hangs straight down from a curled hand, with the tip lost behind the lid, and 30 % of its right third grades below 8. It will be cut against kitchen_over in the same coverage, and the hands will jump between angles.
fixes.fix: Re-render kitchen at 1280x720 with the current home.py after the hand re-pose (the kitchen_over hands fix above). Check that the mug, envelope, hands and laptop angle match kitchen_over at the cut.

fixes.problem: Gene's hands still read as posed. His left hand lies flat with its fingers fanned wide (family_member() curls it only 4-10 degrees), and his right hand's curled fingertips perch on the plate's rim. Both men's head-and-shoulder silhouettes, cut out of the street light's blind stripes, fall on the end wall. So Ch 10's device, Gene's striped shadow that vanishes with him, already shows in the warm Ch 01 dinner and pulls the eye to the wall. The patch is near neutral, not blue (bright stripes about 54/54/58 RGB above the rail, 50/45/45 on the panelling). The pattern leaks, not the colour.
fixes.fix:
1. In family_member(), curl Gene2014's left hand 25-35 degrees at MCP and PIP, close its fan with articulate_hand's spread value, and rest it at the table edge.
2. Give his right hand the glass in front of his plate, the way Tim's hand holds his cup, or rest it beside the plate rather than on its rim.
3. For the family layout, lower street further (0.10 today, to about 0.03-0.05) or light-link it away from the figures, so the end wall carries the warm pendant falloff instead of the striped silhouettes. Leave it as it is in the gene layout, where the striped shadow is the device.
